title: Golden Triangle (Delhi–Agra–Jaipur)
selection: The Delhi–Agra–Jaipur Golden Triangle links the three most-visited destinations in north India: Delhi (an estimated 2.0 million foreign tourist visits in 2024), Uttar Pradesh (2.27 million) and Rajasthan (2.07 million), and includes six UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

itineraries.title: Golden Triangle in 5 days: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur
itineraries.summary: One day in Delhi, the Gatimaan Express to Agra for the fort and a sunset view of the Taj, the Taj at sunrise and Fatehpur Sikri on the way to Jaipur, two Jaipur days, then back to Delhi.
itineraries.seoTitle: Golden Triangle 5-Day Itinerary: Delhi, Agra, Jaipur
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic 5-day Golden Triangle with real times: Gatimaan to Agra, the Taj at sunrise, Fatehpur Sikri on the 240 km road to Jaipur, and Amber Fort.

plan.overview: The classic loop in five days, with every long leg in the morning. Day 1 is Old Delhi and Humayun's Tomb. Day 2 takes the Gatimaan Express to Agra for the fort, the 'Baby Taj' and a sunset view of the Taj from Mehtab Bagh. Day 3 is the Taj at sunrise, then the road to Jaipur with a stop at Fatehpur Sikri. Day 4 is Jaipur's hill forts; Day 5 the old city before the drive back to Delhi. Check the weekdays: Day 1 can't be a Monday, and Days 2 and 3 can't be Fridays.
plan.season: October to March is best: mild days, though winter fog can delay trains and Delhi's air is often poor from October to February. April–June is very hot.
plan.transport: Gatimaan Express Delhi → Agra; car with driver Agra → Jaipur → Delhi.

budget.assumptions: Per adult, entry fees only; hotels, car and train fares vary by season and class.

Hire one car Agra → Jaipur → Delhi; agree the Fatehpur Sikri stop and the driver's allowance.
Buy online through the ASI; the Taj is closed on Fridays.

alternatives: Prefer to fly home from Jaipur? Skip the Day 5 drive and fly from Jaipur International Airport.
Seven days? Add a second Delhi day and a slower Agra — see the seven-day plan.
tips: Check the weekdays: the Red Fort is closed on Mondays, and the Taj Mahal and Gatimaan Express on Fridays.
See the Taj at sunrise — the official site recommends early visits; sunset is busier.
Hawa Mahal closes at 4:30 pm; go before the City Palace if you're short of time.

prep.title: Taj Mahal rules
prep.body: Food, tobacco, chargers, headphones and tripods aren't allowed; carry little. Polluting vehicles can't go within 500 m, so you'll take a battery bus or golf cart from the car park.

prep.title: Scams
prep.body: Ignore touts near Delhi stations who say your train has moved or that you need a 'boarding pass' to enter; buy tickets only at official counters or online.

faqs.q: Is 5 days enough for the Golden Triangle?
faqs.a: Yes, at a steady pace: one day in Delhi, two in Agra (with Fatehpur Sikri on the way out) and two in Jaipur.

faqs.q: How far is Agra from Jaipur?
faqs.a: About 240 km via Bharatpur, 4–5 hours by road; Fatehpur Sikri is on the way.

itineraries.seoDescription: Seven days on the Golden Triangle: Old and New Delhi, the Gatimaan to Agra, the Taj at sunrise, Fatehpur Sikri, then Jaipur's old city, forts and bazaars.

plan.overview: The Golden Triangle at a pace that leaves time to look. Two Delhi days split Old Delhi from the Mughal and Sultanate south. Day 3 takes the Gatimaan Express to Agra for the fort, the 'Baby Taj' and Mehtab Bagh at sunset; Day 4 is the Taj at sunrise and Fatehpur Sikri on the road to Jaipur. Jaipur gets two full days — the walled city, then the hill forts — and a last morning in the bazaars before the drive back to Delhi.

stops.note: Garden aligned with the Taj across the river; sunset view.

days.travel: Delhi → Agra by train (about 1 hour 40 minutes) or road (about 230 km); short cab rides in Agra.
days.driveTime: About 2 hours by train, or 3–4 hours by road
days.meals: Lunch in Agra; Mughlai dinner and petha.

days.title: Taj Mahal at sunrise, Fatehpur Sikri, on to Jaipur
days.summary: The Taj at first light, Akbar's red-sandstone capital, then the road to Jaipur.

stops.name: Taj Mahal
stops.note: Opens 30 minutes before sunrise; closed Fridays. Use the east or west gate.

stops.name: Fatehpur Sikri
stops.note: About 37 km from Agra: Buland Darwaza and Salim Chishti's tomb.

stops.name: Drive to Jaipur
stops.note: Via Bharatpur; arrive by early evening.

days.travel: Agra → Jaipur about 240 km via Bharatpur (4–5 hours); Fatehpur Sikri is on the way.
days.meals: Breakfast in Agra; lunch near Fatehpur Sikri.

days.title: Jaipur: the walled city
days.summary: Palace, observatory, the Palace of Winds and the museum lit up at night.

stops.name: City Palace
stops.note: Composite ticket (₹500) also covers Jaigarh tomorrow.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal
stops.note: Closes 4:30 pm.

stops.name: Albert Hall Museum (lit up)
stops.note: Evening session 7–9:30 pm.

days.travel: All within the walled city and Ram Niwas Garden.

days.title: Jaipur: Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh
days.summary: The hill forts along the ridge.

stops.name: Amber Fort
stops.note: Suraj Pol, Jaleb Chowk and the Sheesh Mahal.

stops.name: Jaigarh Fort
stops.note: About 2.5 km above Amber; the Jaivana cannon.

stops.name: Nahargarh Fort
stops.note: Views over Jaipur at dusk.

days.travel: City → Amber about 11 km; Nahargarh is about 6 km from the city by the fort road.
days.meals: Lunch in Amer or the city.

days.title: Jaipur's bazaars, then back to Delhi
days.summary: A last morning in the markets and the drive north.

stops.name: Johari Bazaar and Bapu Bazaar
stops.note: Jewellery and textiles; mojaris at Bapu.

stops.name: Drive to Delhi
stops.note: About 268 km.
